headline: SILVER SURGES 20% IN AUGUST TO $70, SENDS MINERS SOARING — First Majestic +42%, Fresnillo Triples H1 Profit as 6th Consecutive Deficit Year Tightens Supply
snippet: Silver reached US$70 per ounce in August — its strongest monthly advance in modern history at 20% and up 73.76% year-over-year — before easing to $69 ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. Mexico-exposed producers led the equity surge: First Majestic Silver (NYSE: AG) gained 42% in August alone while Fresnillo nearly tripled first-half profit despite lower Mexican output and Avino Silver posted outsized leverage to spot prices. The rally comes as the Silver Institute confirms 2026 marks the sixth consecutive year of a structural global silver supply deficit, with above-ground stocks depleted and industrial demand from solar panels, EV motors, and AI-data-center infrastructure outpacing mine supply by a widening margin.

headline: NEXGEN EXTENDS PCE URANIUM ZONE 17% DEEPER TO 644m, DEPLOYS FIFTH DRILL RIG — Best Two 2026 Holes Rank Among Top Three Ever Drilled at Athabasca Discovery
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX: NXE, ASX: NXG) released summer 2026 drilling results from its Patterson Corridor East discovery in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, expanding the high-grade subdomain's vertical extent by 17% to 644 metres with mineralization now confirmed to 930 metres depth. Highlights include hole RK-26-293 returning 4.7 metres above 10,000 counts per second and hole RK-26-296 extending the up-dip high-grade subdomain by 50 metres along strike. The two best 2026 holes rank as the best and third-best holes ever drilled at PCE since discovery, and NexGen is deploying a fifth drill rig to accelerate the 42,000-metre program alongside construction of the adjacent Rook I project.

headline: ZINC AT 4-YEAR HIGH AS LME WAREHOUSE STOCKS COLLAPSE 64% — $174 Backwardation Enters 7th Straight Day, Signals Tightest Physical Metal Since 2022
snippet: LME zinc settled at $4,107 per tonne on August 27 — its highest since June 2022 and up 55% from the mid-2025 trough — as available warehouse stocks fell from 264,000 tonnes in December 2024 to roughly 95,000 tonnes, a 64% drawdown. A backwardation of $174 per tonne (prompt metal commands a $174 premium over three-month forward prices) marks one of the clearest physical tightness signals in the LME's recent history, reflecting mine supply disruptions and accelerating demand from galvanizing and zinc-rich battery chemistries. The sustained rally has re-ignited interest in zinc junior miners on the TSX-V, particularly those with projects in Canada, Australia, and Namibia.

headline: KORYX COPPER DRILLS 969m FROM SURFACE AT HAIB, NAMIBIA — HM185 Returns 236m at 0.51% Cu in One of Deposit's Best Intersections Yet; Pre-FS on Track Year-End
snippet: Koryx Copper (TSX-V: KRY) released assay results from 19 drill holes totalling 8,586 metres at its Haib copper project in southern Namibia, with hole HM167 intersecting 969 metres of continuous copper-molybdenum-gold mineralization from surface at 0.23% Cu — the longest continuously mineralized intersection in the project's history — and HM185 returning 236 metres at 0.51% Cu within a broader 413-metre interval at 0.37% Cu, one of Haib's best intersections by contained metal. All 19 holes intersected thick mineralization at or above the average MRE grade, supporting a pending resource update and prefeasibility study expected before year-end at one of Africa's largest undeveloped copper porphyry deposits.

headline: CABRAL GOLD OPENS NEW JERIMUM CIMA ZONE 200m SOUTH OF MAIN TARGET — 8.9m at 5.8 g/t Au in DDH411 Weeks Before September Heap Leach First-Gold Pour
snippet: Cabral Gold (TSXV: CBR) reported that drill hole DDH411 intersected a new mineralized zone at the Jerimum Cima target within its Cuiú Cuiú Gold Project in Pará, Brazil — returning 8.9 metres at 5.8 g/t gold from 208 metres depth, including 1.8 metres at 28.4 g/t gold — located 200 metres south of the main zone and pointing to multiple parallel discovery corridors. The result comes just weeks before the company plans to pour its first gold from a heap leach oxide starter pit at the Moreira Gomes target, with commercial production targeted for Q4 2026 — making Cabral one of the rare TSXV names simultaneously approaching cash flow while opening new resource upside at the same project.

headline: FORGE REPLACES MINERALS SECURITY PARTNERSHIP AS ALLIED CRITICAL MINERALS HUB — G7-Plus Nations Overhaul Framework as China Controls 85% of Global Rare Earth Refining
snippet: The Minerals Security Partnership (MSP) is being superseded by FORGE — a new allied critical minerals coordination framework chaired by South Korea — in what analysts describe as a significant escalation of how the US, EU, Japan, Korea, Australia, and Canada coordinate supply chain security against Chinese dominance of rare earth, lithium, and battery metal refining. The restructuring reflects strategic frustration with the MSP's pace and signals a push for binding trade mechanisms, offtake coordination, and financing guarantees for Western-aligned mining projects — with direct implications for Canadian, Australian, and allied-nation junior miners seeking government-backed project financing.

headline: SILVER BREAKOUT OR BLOW-OFF? ANALYSTS DEBATE WHETHER $70 HIGH HOLDS INTO Q4 — Sixth-Year Deficit Meets Stretched Futures Positioning Ahead of Warsh's Rate Signal
snippet: With silver up 20% in August and 73% year-over-year, analysts are split on whether the metal's assault on $70 per ounce represents a durable structural breakout or a short-term blow-off that will correct once Warsh's Jackson Hole tone clarifies the rate path. The bull case rests on a sixth consecutive year of physical supply deficit, depleted above-ground stocks, and industrial demand from solar, EVs, and AI infrastructure accelerating beyond mine supply response. The bear case cites a potentially strengthening dollar if Warsh signals September tightening and speculative positioning in COMEX silver futures at historically stretched levels.

headline: SPROTT: GOLD AND SILVER STRUCTURAL BULL INTACT BEYOND 2026 CORRECTION — Western Capital Rotation Yet to Begin as Central Banks Hold All-Time Record Reserves
snippet: Sprott's latest precious metals outlook argues that the corrections in gold and silver through the first half of 2026 were healthy consolidations within a secular bull market — pointing to central bank gold holdings reaching an all-time record, physical silver deficits compounding for the sixth consecutive year, and western generalist capital having barely begun to rotate into precious metals despite record producer margins. The analysis identifies the current setup as historically similar to mid-2010, when gold and silver built bases before their final parabolic advances, with today's macro backdrop of negative real yields, accelerating money supply growth, and geopolitical fragmentation providing a more structurally supportive foundation.

headline: EIA ANNUAL URANIUM MARKET REPORT: PRICES HOLD STEADY AT $87.55/LB AS UTILITIES SHIFT TO LONG-TERM CONTRACTS — Structural Deficit Deepening Through 2030s
snippet: The U.S. Energy Information Administration's annual uranium market report shows spot prices holding at $87.55 per pound in late August 2026, with utilities pausing spot purchases in favour of multi-year long-term supply security agreements as they race to lock in supply ahead of a projected deepening structural deficit through the 2030s. Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom and Canada's Cameco confirm 2026 production targets remain on track, but the report flags that global mine pipelines are insufficient to match accelerating reactor build demand — particularly from AI-data-centre-powered nuclear baseload growth in the US, UK, and Japan — keeping the long-term price above $90 per pound.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC SILVER RAISES 2026 GUIDANCE SECOND TIME ON RECORD COAHUILA AND SONORA THROUGHPUT — Stock +42% In August as Operational Gains Compound Price Rally
snippet: First Majestic Silver (NYSE: AG, TSX: AG) has raised its 2026 silver production guidance for the second consecutive time this year following a record second-quarter throughput performance at its Coahuila and Sonora operations in Mexico, adding approximately 500,000 silver-equivalent ounces to the year's output target. The guidance raise — a rare demonstration of operational delivery on top of a commodity tailwind — drove the stock up 42% in August, outperforming silver's own 20% monthly gain and highlighting the leverage that an operationally improving producer carries at current prices. Four Mexican mines produced 3.8 million ounces of silver and 34,660 ounces of gold in the second quarter.
